parts.text: For Examiner’s Use In this experiment, you will investigate the stretching of a spring. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 1.1 and Fig. 1.2. Do not move the large load that is on the bench. At the start of the experiment, the spring should not be attached to the forcemeter. forcemeter spring load bench unstretched spring load bench clamp Fig. 1.1 Fig. 1.2

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) Measure the unstretched length l 0 of the spring , in mm. l 0 = ................................................mm

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) On Fig. 1.1 , mark clearly the distance you have measured.

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Attach the spring to the forcemeter, as shown in Fig. 1.2. The load must remain on the bench.

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Gently raise the forcemeter until it reads 1.0 N. Clamp the forcemeter in this position. Record the forcemeter reading F in Table 1.1. Measure, and record in the table, the new length l of the spring.

parts.label: v
parts.text: (v) Calculate the extension e of the spring using the equation e = ( l – l 0 ). Record the value of e in the table.

parts.label: vi
parts.text: For Examiner’s Use (vi) Repeat steps (iv) and (v) using forcemeter readings of 2.0 N, 3.0 N, 4.0 N and 5.0 N. Record all the readings and results in the table. Table 1.1 F / N l / mm e / mm [4]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Plot a graph of e / mm ( y -axis) against F / N ( x -axis). [4]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = ................................................. [2]
